edits.title: Let the two-point line become a recorder
edits.old: Each accepted position occupies a place in that ordered list. The recorder joins neighbouring positions with straight segments. Enough small segments can let us see a curve. Go closer to a turn: the smooth-looking gesture has acquired joints. The connection between two samples has been drawn; it is not a measurement of everything your hand did between them.[^point-trace-sampling]
edits.new: `_trail_points` holds positions in the order they were kept; `size()` counts them. The recorder joins each position to the next with a straight segment. Repeated in small enough steps, the two-point construction from the last room lets us see a curve. The gesture has acquired joints. Between those joints, the program draws a connection; your hand may have taken another way.[^point-trace-sampling]
edits.incitement: Give the existing code a plain reading and carry the previous hall's segment into this new capability. Keep the difference between a sampled bend and its constructed joins visible.
edits.purpose: Explain the list count and how repeated straight connections form a visible curve without recording every intervening movement.
edits.reader_move: Read the count operation and consider what was drawn between two retained positions.
edits.why_here: The reader has made a loop and seen the count; a familiar construction can now explain how the record becomes a line.
edits.without: The list operation remains partly implicit and the new capability can seem disconnected from the two-point segment.

edits.title: Keep the time of waiting distinct from the count
edits.old: The dot waits for at least five millimetres of movement before considering another sample. Below that movement threshold, the update can return without adding a position. A stationary pause can leave the list unchanged while Point One's counter has plenty more calls to count.
edits.new: The dot compares its present position with the one where it last passed the movement test. Less than five millimetres apart, and no new position is added. A still pause can leave the count unchanged while Point One's counter keeps running. You spend time holding the line still; the position list does not say how long you waited.
edits.incitement: Explain what the five millimetres are measured from, then let the pause acquire its own consequence: elapsed waiting is absent from this position-only list.
edits.purpose: Make the movement comparison understandable and distinguish the continuing time of a held pause from the retained position count.
edits.reader_move: Watch a still pause and ask what in the record could report its duration.
edits.why_here: Answers the opening pause experiment and returns to the counter without treating all running loops as identical records.
edits.without: Movement threshold remains programming vocabulary and the pause's unrecorded duration stays implicit.

edits.title: Watch a row leave the window
edits.old: Read two neighbouring rows. The coordinates give places in world metres. If your loop has more than ten points, its first row may have left the table: the instrument shows the last ten, while the larger count names the whole retained list. The line can hold something its small window is no longer showing.
edits.new: Read two neighbouring rows. Each gives three coordinates, in world metres, for a retained position. When the count reaches eleven, the table starts at row 2: it has room to show only the last ten. The drawing still has its beginning. What has left the screen has not yet left the line.
edits.incitement: Use one exact count to distinguish the visible table from the stored drawing. Leaving the display is not yet deletion from the list.
edits.purpose: Explain the last-ten window through the eleven-point case while retaining the difference between display and storage.
edits.reader_move: Compare a retained count with the numbered rows currently visible.
edits.why_here: After learning what enters the list, inspect the narrower account supplied by its screen.
edits.without: The windowing behavior stays conditional and less easy to picture or verify.
